items.followUp: Define the proportional limit of a material.

rubric.why: Identifies that the body returns to its original state.
rubric.description: States that the body regains its original shape and size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body returns to its original shape and size.

rubric.why: Specifies the condition under which elastic recovery occurs and identifies the limiting point.
rubric.description: Explains that this happens when the deforming force is removed, up to the elastic limit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking recovery after removal of the force to the elastic limit.

modelAnswer: The elastic limit is the greatest value of deforming force up to which a body regains its original shape and size when the force is removed.

rubric.why: Identifies the quantity a thermometer measures.
rubric.description: States that a thermometer measures temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying temperature.

rubric.why: Identifies a thermometer as a measuring device.
rubric.description: Describes it as an instrument used to measure temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as an instrument or device.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.

items.followUp: State Newton’s first law of motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Gives the central relationship in Newton’s second law.
rubric.description: States that force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the proportionality between force and the rate of change of momentum.

rubric.why: Includes the direction specified by the law.
rubric.description: States that the change in momentum is in the direction of the applied force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying the direction of the change in momentum.

rubric.why: Shows the mathematical form of the law or its result for constant mass.
rubric.description: Writes the force–momentum relation and uses constant mass to obtain the acceleration form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct mathematical relation, including F=ma.

rubric.why: Completes the derivation to the standard equation of motion.
rubric.description: Uses acceleration as change in velocity per unit time and gives F=ma (with proportionality constant taken as one in SI units).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting acceleration to the momentum relation and stating F=ma.

modelAnswer: Newton’s second law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of that force.
Momentum, p = mv.
For a body of constant mass, change in momentum = mv − mu = m(v − u).
Rate of change of momentum = m(v − u)/t.
Since a = (v − u)/t, rate of change of momentum = ma.
Therefore, F ∝ ma.
In SI units, the proportionality constant is 1; hence F = ma.

items.followUp: A vehicle increases its velocity from 5 m s⁻¹ to 25 m s⁻¹ in 10 s. Find its acceleration.

rubric.why: Correctly identifies the initial and final velocities and time.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying u, v and t.

rubric.why: Selects a valid equation for constant acceleration.
rubric.description: Uses the acceleration equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given values correctly with units.
rubric.description: Substitutes the data into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution.

rubric.why: Checks the numerical evaluation.
rubric.description: Calculates the acceleration as 2.5.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical value.

rubric.why: Checks that acceleration is expressed in SI units.
rubric.description: Gives the answer with the correct unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m s⁻².

modelAnswer: Given: u = 0 m s⁻¹, v = 20 m s⁻¹, t = 8 s.
Formula: a = (v − u)/t.
Substitution: a = (20 m s⁻¹ − 0 m s⁻¹)/8 s.
Calculation: a = 20/8 m s⁻² = 2.5 m s⁻².
Answer: The acceleration of the car is 2.5 m s⁻².

items.followUp: Derive the equation for gravitational potential energy near Earth’s surface.

rubric.why: Defines kinetic energy by relating it to motion.
rubric.description: Defines kinetic energy as energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Starts the derivation using work and Newton’s second law.
rubric.description: Writes work done as force times displacement and uses F=ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for these starting relations.

rubric.why: Uses the kinematic relation to express displacement for a body starting from rest.
rubric.description: Applies v² − u² = 2as with initial velocity zero, giving s = v²/(2a).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct kinematic step.

rubric.why: Recognizes the final expression for kinetic energy.
rubric.description: Substitutes into work done and obtains K.E. = ½mv².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct derived equation.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Work done, W = Fs.
For a body starting from rest, v² − u² = 2as and u = 0.
Therefore, s = v²/(2a).
Since F = ma, W = Fs = ma × v²/(2a).
Thus, kinetic energy, K.E. = W = ½mv².

items.followUp: What is meant by a standard unit?

rubric.why: Shows that physical quantities are measurable.
rubric.description: States that physical quantities can be measured.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying measurability.

rubric.why: States how a physical quantity is expressed.
rubric.description: States that a physical quantity is expressed by a magnitude and a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including magnitude and unit.

modelAnswer: Physical quantities are quantities that can be measured and expressed by a magnitude and a unit.

items.followUp: When is a body said to be in motion?

rubric.why: Identifies the defining property of rest.
rubric.description: States that the body’s position remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its position does not change.

rubric.why: Makes clear that rest is judged over time and relative to a reference.
rubric.description: States that the position remains unchanged with time relative to its surroundings or a reference point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the time and reference frame.

modelAnswer: A body is said to be at rest if its position does not change with time relative to its surroundings or a reference point.

items.followUp: Give one example of a vector quantity and state its direction.

rubric.why: Identifies one defining property of a vector.
rubric.description: States that a vector has magnitude.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for magnitude.

rubric.why: Identifies the other defining property or a vector-specific rule.
rubric.description: States that a vector has direction, or that vectors obey vector addition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for direction or the vector-addition property.

modelAnswer: Vectors are physical quantities that have both magnitude and direction and obey the laws of vector addition.
